title: Canonical derived multiplication for the polynomial Koszul square
statement: Let R be a commutative ring and f:Fin r\to R a Koszul-regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-koszul-regular-sequence]. Let P=ℤ[x_i] (with the universe lift), Z=P/(x_i), I=(f_i), and B=R/I. Form the square (P\to Z)\to (R\to B), sending x_i to f_i and integers to their quotient classes. Its canonical derived multiplication Z\otimes ᴸ_P R\to B[0], defined as the adjunct of the actual square module map under [lem-trf-cotangent-flat-base-change], is invertible.

source.place: Tag 08SJ (lemma-mod-regular-sequence), first paragraph: the polynomial Koszul square and derived tensor identification.

proof.text: Construct the commutative polynomial square by evaluation and identify the zero-section quotient P/(x_i) with ℤ via evaluation at zero. Identify the mixed tensor with second argument R[0] with ordinary scalar extension by the tensor-unit isomorphism.

Use the pointwise mixed-tensor derived functor. Transport universality of the scalar-extension counit from homotopy localization to cochains. Uniqueness of right Kan extensions identifies these two derived functors; the Koszul derived-quotient comparison then gives an isomorphism e from the derived extension of Z[0] to B[0]. This step requires no normalization of e.

Let μ be the canonical derived multiplication. Full faithfulness of the derived single functor writes e⁻¹μ as the single of an R-linear endomorphism k of B. The adjunct of e similarly comes from a P-linear map a:Z→Res(B). Naturality of the adjunction and of the restriction/single comparison gives a followed by k equal to the square module map. Evaluating at 1 yields k(a(1))=1.

An R-linear endomorphism k of R/I is multiplication by k(1), since R→R/I is surjective. If k(x)=1, then x·k(1)=1; multiplication by x is its inverse. Thus k and hence μ=e∘single(k) are isomorphisms. This covers r=0, the unit ideal, and the zero ring.
